Commentary.Commentary: We are back for South Africa's reply with the bat. The two umpires and players have made their way out to the centre. Aiden Markram and Quinton de Kock are the two openers for South Africa. Matthew Forde will open the attack for the Men in Maroon. Markram on strike.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Looking ahead - South Africa will be slightly disappointed that they allowed the West Indies off the hook after having their foot firmly on the throat. Even so, they will feel confident about chasing this down. On this red soil surface, there has been little to suggest that batting is particularly challenging. The pitch has played true for the most part, without any major demons. West Indies will be on the hunt for early wickets to put South Africa on the back foot. Stay tuned for the chase!

From loose to lethal - It was an indifferent start from South Africa, conceding 29 runs in the first two overs and putting down a couple of chances as well. Despite that shaky beginning, they managed to strike back strongly, picking up four wickets inside the Powerplay. Just as he did in the game against India, Aiden Markram kept ringing the changes intelligently, and his quicks did not disappoint him.

Shepherd and Holder script the rescue - After being asked to bat first, West Indies did not give themselves the best chance to score on this surface. Having played their previous games in Mumbai and Kolkata before arriving in Ahmedabad, they found the steep bounce tough to tackle, and it played a significant role in several of the dismissals. Yet the Windies refused to rein in their attacking instincts. No one took the responsibility to play themselves in and stabilise the innings until Romario Shepherd and Jason Holder combined to engineer a recovery for their side.

Good execution at the death from South Africa - Just 13 runs came off the last 2 overs. West Indies will take 176, considering that they were 83/7 at one stage and staring down the barrel. The 57-ball 89-run stand between Romario Shepherd and Jason Holder has helped them get to a competitive total.

FOUR! A streaky boundary to finish the innings! Corbin Bosch bowls this in the blockhole, on middle and leg. Romario Shepherd moves to the leg side and gets his bat down in time. It takes the inside edge and races to the fine leg fence for four runs. Shepherd also brings up his FIFTY on the last ball. West Indies finish on 176/8!

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS! You won't see such a chaotic, yet entertaining start to a match. We have had everything so far. The first 2 overs went for 29 runs, but then South Africa struck back, taking 4/14 despite dropping a couple of catches. West Indies are in a tough spot here, and this pair of Sherfane Rutherford and Rovman Powell need to take this game deep, as they still have a lot of firepower left in the tank. South Africa will want to just keep the pressure on the batters and not give away anything loose, keep picking up wickets, and they will have a real chance of getting the Windies bowled out cheaply. Also, Corbin Bosch is to bowl after the break.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match formalities! The Proteas spread out under the hot sun and take up the fielding positions. Brandon King and Shai Hope are the two openers for West Indies. We will see spin straightaway as Keshav Maharaj has the new ball in hand. Let's play...

It is time for the unfurling of the flags of both countries. Now we see players from both sides make their way out to the middle and line up for their respective national anthems. It will be South Africa's first, followed by that of West Indies.

PITCH REPORT - Former West Indies leggie, Samuel Badree, is pitchside. He says that it is quite hot out there and the temperature will remain around the mid 30s. Adds that if you are bowling from the North End, the square boundaries are 60 and 70 meters, while the straight hit is 72 meters. Former South African fast bowler, Shaun Pollock, joins him and says that it is a red soil pitch, so we can expect steeper bounce and a bit of turn as well. Shares that 53 per cent of wickets for the pacers have come on slower balls, and he expects that trend to continue here.

We would have bowled first as well - The skipper of West Indies, Shai Hope starts off by saying that they wanted to bowl first as well, but he thinks his team will do just as fine while batting first. Continues that they have one change in the playing XI with Roston Chase coming in for Akeal Hosein. Adds that it is a tactical change because of the opposition and the conditions. Ends up saying that they have to play their best cricket today, and he hopes that their momentum carries forward as well.

Execution is key - South Africa's captain, Aiden Markram says that it looks like a good wicket. Adds that they have played here one or two games ago and he hopes that the moisture on the pitch settles down and makes batting easier later. Mentions that they have been lucky to play a few games here, but every wicket has been different, the one they played against India was completely different from this one. Tells that it all comes down to execution at the end. Markram shares that Rabada has been leading from the front. His contributions are not only limited to the numbers, but behind the scenes, he brings value and experience, and also playing here in IPL helps a bit as well. Informs that they are unchanged.

South Africa (Unchanged Playing XI) - Aiden Markram (C), Quinton de Kock (WK), Ryan Rickelton, Dewald Brevis, David Miller, Tristan Stubbs, Marco Jansen, Corbin Bosch, Kagiso Rabada, Keshav Maharaj and Lungi Ngidi.

West Indies (Playing XI) - Shai Hope (C/WK), Brandon King, Shimron Hetmyer, Rovman Powell, Sherfane Rutherford, Roston Chase (In for Akeal Hosein), Jason Holder, Romario Shepherd, Matthew Forde, Gudakesh Motie and Shamar Joseph.
TOSS - Time for the flip of the coin. Aiden Markram and Shai Hope are present in the centre. 'Tails' is the call from Markram, and he gets it right. South Africa elect to BOWL first.

What it means for the other two teams - India and Zimbabwe, both bruised from their opening Super 8 defeats, do not currently have qualification in their hands. That, however, could change within a few hours. If South Africa win today, India will know that victories in their remaining two matches will be enough to see them through. Similarly, if the West Indies prevail, Zimbabwe will have a clear equation. Two wins from their remaining games would send the Chevrons into the semi-finals without worrying about net run rate. That makes it clear where loyalties will lie in this afternoon's clash. Stick around for the toss and team news.

Battle of the unbeaten - Neither South Africa nor the West Indies have lost a match at this World Cup, which makes this contest even more compelling. Their emphatic wins in the Super 8s opener mean that a victory today would put the victor within touching distance of a semi-final berth. The West Indies hold a slight edge thanks to a formidable net run rate of +5.350, while South Africa are not far behind with a NRR of +3.8.

Greetings, all - Welcome to an important day in the race for the semi-finals in Group 1. Two pivotal games are lined up, and both carry significant weight in shaping the path to the last four. First up, it is South Africa taking on the West Indies in Ahmedabad, before we head south to Chennai, where India and Zimbabwe lock horns later in the day.
... MATCH DAY ...

High stakes showdown - The second round of fixtures in Group 1 kicks off with South Africa taking on the West Indies at Ahmedabad's Narendra Modi Stadium. Two teams that began their Super 8 campaign with statement wins will now look to take a decisive step towards the semi-finals. Fortress Ahmedabad - Ahmedabad has turned into quite the fortress for the Proteas. The 2024 runners-up look determined to go all the way this time after the heartbreak in Barbados. Unbeaten so far, four of South Africa's five games have come at this venue, and they have made it their stronghold. The win over reigning champions India would have injected enormous belief into the side. Different individuals have stepped up at different times, with David Miller, Dewald Brevis and Tristan Stubbs making telling contributions against India. Their top three, though, have been slightly inconsistent. Ryan Rickelton and Quinton de Kock are yet to fully hit their stride, while Aiden Markram has been the more consistent presence at the top. With the ball, Marco Jansen and Lungi Ngidi have led the pace attack and compensated for the underwhelming returns from Kagiso Rabada, who has just two wickets in five games with a strike rate of 59, the worst among the Proteas bowlers. Corbin Bosch and Keshav Maharaj have chipped in as well, and alongside Markram, Maharaj will have a key role to play in the spin department. Caribbean charge - West Indies lead the standings in Group 1 after a thumping 107-run win over Zimbabwe in Mumbai and have carried that momentum from the group stage into the Super 8s. Confidence is high, and their net run rate boost has put them in a strong position early in this phase. The Men in Maroon have never played a T20I in Ahmedabad. That unfamiliarity could be a factor, and they will have to lean on the experience of players who have played at this venue in the IPL. There remains a concern at the top of the order, with Brandon King yet to make a truly impactful contribution. However, the middle order has fired consistently enough to ensure it has not hampered their campaign. Is it time for Johnson Charles to come in for King? Over his career, he has enjoyed success against South Africa, and his highest T20I score of 118 came against the Proteas. One of the big positives for the Caribbean side after their previous win was Rovman Powell getting crucial runs under his belt. In the spin department, Gudakesh Motie has been among the standouts. Fellow left-arm finger spinner Akeal Hosein also had a good day out against Zimbabwe, which are encouraging signs heading into this clash. On the pace bowling front, it has been a collective effort. Jason Holder, Matthew Forde, Romario Shepherd and Shamar Joseph have all contributed at different stages, giving the West Indies variety and depth with the ball. Form (Last 5 completed T20Is, most recent first) - South Africa - WWWWW | West Indies - WWWWW. What to expect? Ahmedabad has hosted five games so far at this World Cup, but this will be the first afternoon fixture with a 3 pm start. The heat will be a major factor early on, with both sides having to manage the conditions before temperatures ease a bit after sunset. With dew not being a factor, the toss may not carry as much weight as it does in evening matches. There is also recent history between these two sides. Just before the start of the World Cup, they faced off in a T20I series in South Africa, which the hosts won 2-1. In T20 World Cup meetings, the Proteas have had the upper hand, winning four out of five clashes, including the last two. All signs point to a fiercely contested afternoon in Ahmedabad. Who are you rooting for?
